statement.p: Use the Chain Rule to calculate the partial derivatives
Express your answer in terms of the independent variables u,v

static.solution: g(x,y)=\cos\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) are \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}=-2x\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) \quad \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}=-2y\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) The partial derivatives of x,y and z with respect to s are \frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{u}}=-3 \quad \frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{v}}=2 \frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{u}}=4 \quad \frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{v}}=1 We use the Chain Rule to find the following derivative: \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{u}}= \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}\frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{u}}+ \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}\frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{u}} =-\left(8y-6x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)= =-\left(50u-4v\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(25u^{2}+5v^{2}-4uv\right) \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{v}}= \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}\frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{v}}+ \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}\frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{v}} =-\left(4x+2y\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)= =-\left(10v-4u\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(25u^{2}+5v^{2}-4uv\right)
